Definition: from G5228 and the base of G188; beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth:--+ pass the flower of (her) age.
BiblicalUsage: hypérakmos is the word for past the flower of age, beyond youth. In 1 Corinthians 7:36, the text says "if she pass the flower of [her] age."
TheologicalSignificance: This word, hypérakmos, does its job quietly — past the flower of age, beyond youth — and I leave it at that.
